findings.title: Step 3 item 6 appends `git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>` for every untracked, unignored fenced file, so an unignored `.env` or key file is written whole into `input-diff.patch`, which is committed and handed to every agent.
findings.name: Secret In Patch

findings.title: File names and config strings are typed raw into Bash command lines (review.md:71, :104, :155, :164, :212, :217, :222; dispatch.md:160 to 162, :242; gate-auditor.md:90 to 92; proof-runner.md:147 `{file}`), so a name holding `'`, `$(` or a space breaks the command or runs as shell.
findings.name: Raw Names In Shell

findings.title: The only memory limit on a proof run is `--max-old-space-size`, which bounds the V8 heap and not Buffer or ArrayBuffer memory, and the half-of-total check at :70 to 72 counts one cap for a file that may start several node children, so the agent's claim to protect the machine does not hold.
findings.name: Heap Only Cap

findings.title: gate-auditor, data-contract-reviewer (:268) and live-system-reviewer (:334) write their own `## Round <n-1> status` and hold the only RESOLVED rules for their domains, while dispatch.md:264 to 266 tells them not to re-verify and synthesis.md:111 to 131 builds the one status table without those rules; five older agents and known-bugchecker.md:117 (blast radius) use three other words for the same job.
findings.name: Round Status Clash

findings.title: proof-runner's HIGH and MEDIUM findings (CAPPED, TIMEOUT, tree changed) reach no consumer: synthesis.md:52 to 55 reads the Proof table only, dispatch.md:280 to 282 hands proof.md over as "not a status", dispatch Step 7 has no branch on `Stopped:`, and the dispatch ledger line carries no STOPPED word.
findings.name: Orphaned Proof Findings

findings.title: The accessibility trigger regex matches only `\x1b[` and `\u001b[`, missing `\033[`, `\e[` and color libraries, while ux-reviewer.md:106 to 109 now files color-only meaning as an untiered REC to accessibility-reviewer, so the colorblind hard rule on terminal output can no longer reach a blocking tier.
findings.name: Terminal Color Blindspot

findings.title: The fixer's own narrowed test run carries a heap cap only when dispatch pastes `proof.heap_mb`, and dispatch.md:39 reads `proof` only under `--prove`, so on every plain dispatch dispatch.md:136 pastes `none` and the fixer runs tests with no cap.
findings.name: Uncapped Fixer Tests

findings.title: The landing lane runs `test_cmd` automatically after "go" with no heap cap, no timeout and no memory check, while CONTRACTS.md:222 and templates/config.yaml:90 describe `proof.heap_mb` as the cap for every test process.
findings.name: Uncapped Landing Lane

findings.title: The hand-mutant grep covers only the fixed files and stops only on a changed line, so a mutant already committed in a fixed file, or one in the test file about to run, is run and can read as PASS.
findings.name: Narrow Mutant Grep

findings.title: The pre-run screen reads only the chosen file and refuses only browser drivers and `npm`, `npx`, `git`, installer or build spawns, so a one-hop helper that starts a browser, a node child with its own `--max-old-space-size` or its own `env`, a non-node child, a network or billed API call (the game repo tools/meshy.mjs), or a `.env` read runs as the owner, and neither the dispatch plan (dispatch.md:98 to 99) nor the prompt says a file runs with the owner's environment.
findings.name: Narrow Proof Screen

findings.title: The runner check asks only that `{heap_mb}` and `{file}` appear, so a template with `cd x && node ...`, `npm run build && ...` or an inert `{heap_mb}` passes, runs outside `timeout` or the cap, and :152 then drops `NODE_OPTIONS` for a non-node runner.
findings.name: Loose Runner Template

findings.title: Untracked files enter the fence with no count or size limit, so an unignored `node_modules/` or `.venv/` puts thousands of paths into every agent prompt and every file's source into the patch, fires most conditional triggers, and can pass ARG_MAX on the pathspec greps.
findings.name: Untracked Flood

findings.title: The tree snapshot reads raw `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` into context before the first run and after every run, and the stop rule pastes both outputs, so a repo with many untracked files floods the agent before it writes the report.
findings.name: Snapshot Floods Context

findings.title: The scope-leak listing is taken after the landing lane and proof-runner run, so files those test runs write are named fixer scope leaks and added to the round fence.
findings.name: Test Output As Leaks

findings.title: gate-auditor's allowlist reads commit subjects only, so a failure recorded in a commit body (the game repo 2008cdc, bbdbd03) is invisible and a check recorded as failing files as LOW (STALE) instead of the MEDIUM that gate-auditor.md:257 to 259 gives it.
findings.name: Commit Bodies Unread

findings.title: The cost trigger never fires on a test file, and perf-reviewer.md:19 to 23 now hands every OOM to cost-complexity-reviewer, so in a standard scope an OOM in a test lane (the anchor incident's shape) has no agent that tiers it.
findings.name: Unowned Test OOM

findings.title: The live reviewer reads captures and run logs of a third-party system and writes concrete Scenario lines, but its never-write rule covers only secrets, URLs, hostnames and keys, so a client's name, address or case number can land in the committed report and in the `review_copy` outside the repo.
findings.name: Client Data In Report

findings.title: The run call never sets the Bash tool's own timeout, so a harness timeout at or before `proof.timeout_s` can cut the call before the `EXIT=` line and turn a TIMEOUT into a Bash-failure stop.
The tree snapshot cannot see writes to ignored files, content changes to untracked files, or a same-size rewrite of an already modified binary (`git diff` without `--binary`).

The new agents carry the gap-hunter's cited game repo evidence as worked examples (also data-contract-reviewer.md:151, proof-runner.md:249, CONTRACTS.md:120), so replaying them on that evidence measures recall of the prompt, and no replay on an unseen incident exists.
"Do not read `proof` here" leaves the cost-complexity-reviewer block's `proof.heap_mb` (review.md:276) as `none` in every review and every plain dispatch round.
The description claims the `perf` scope and an "unproven" trigger that review.md:46 and :330 do not give it.
integration-reviewer, devils-advocate (:68 to 73) and security-reviewer (:85 to 86) each claim doc and comment truth with no handoff, and ux-reviewer.md:119 and :134 point only at devils-advocate.

Two lane pairs share a line with no handoff sentence: bugs-reviewer and cost-complexity-reviewer on unbounded memory, data-contract-reviewer and gate-auditor on a drift check that compares only generated keys.

The own-sections list misses accessibility-reviewer's UI files, dependency-reviewer's Inputs missing, UNVERIFIED and Replacement verdicts (dependency-reviewer.md:159, blast radius), proof-runner's Limits, Tree and Failure output, and gap-hunter's sections.
The round synthesis prompt carries no scope, expected agents, not-run list or tree-facts path, and the tree-facts path is also missing from the fixer, proof-runner and consolidator prompts.
Index mode keys on a Status line the configured index does not have, and consolidator's `## Untested entries` (consolidator.md:175) has no consumer.
Index mode never checks that an entry belongs to this repo, and its audit-id keys collide across audits.
The template writes `none` and `[]` into `proof.runner`, `test_globs` and `max_files`, whose defaults apply only when absent, so a template copy with only the two caps set marks every file NOT RUN.
Cites `test-strategist.md:18` for a line that now sits at :19.

gate-auditor bans `git status` for rewriting the index while CONTRACTS.md:394 and proof-runner.md:135 call it read only, and gate-auditor's allowed `git diff --name-only HEAD` (:92) refreshes the index the same way.
Section 1 gives gate-auditor LOW and MEDIUM only, while gate-auditor.md:251 to 254 defines a HIGH, which synthesis would move down every time.
A `live` scope round's fence is the union of work sets, not the whole tool that CONTRACTS.md:154 to 156 names, while the agent is still told its fence is the whole tool.
The custom-list guard stops proof-runner but not fixer, and a custom list naming dependency-reviewer or consolidator skips them with no not-run line.
The new handoff reads `data.invariants`, which review.md:271 to 285 pastes only to data-contract-reviewer.
The round prompt gives devils-advocate no goal statement and no round patch, so hunk item 6 re-walks round 1's patch.

Stale prose: the dispatch ledger examples lack `tokens=` and `proof=`, README.md:132 leaves `goal_doc` out of the multiuser gate, and gate-auditor.md:3 and data-contract-reviewer.md:3 omit the `live` exclusion.
"`grep` or `rg` over the repo" allows `rg --pre` and `--search-zip`, which run programs, and a `grep -r` that reads an unignored `.env`.
Tree-facts item 5 builds a regex from a raw base name, so `el`, `index` or `test` flood false import facts and a `(` breaks the grep.

The content triggers grep every fenced file including markdown, so they match their own definitions and prose, and the live trigger fires on a project's own Playwright benches (the game repo tools/bench-*.mjs).
The voice `build_cmd` checks the Conventions repo when `find` returns nothing and crashes on a path with a space.
`proof.max_files` has no ceiling, and each run can put about 20 KB of output into context.
Failure output is copied verbatim into a committed report with no redaction of secrets a test prints.
Nothing checks that `cost.paid_apis[].key` holds an env var name before it is pasted into prompts and a `git grep -F` line.
The `review_copy` path is built from `live.systems[].name` and `live.review_copy` with no sanitizing, so `/` or `..` writes outside the folder.
The web rule lets dependency-reviewer search "public package names" with no test for telling a private or git dependency apart.
ux-reviewer and dependency-reviewer (dependency-reviewer.md:111, blast radius) hold web tools with no data-not-instructions or query-content rule in their own files.
`first_live_run` is asked for and no rule reads it.
With no `ui_paths`, a mark-data module such as the game repo src/viewer/unit-marks.js is sorted "not UI", and nothing asks the owner to set the key.
The projects holding the third-party-page evidence (the automation repo, the extension repo) have no `.djinn/config.yaml`, so the agent's first real run will not be on that evidence.
Hunk item 6 takes a static `goal_doc` as the goal, so a stale one (the game repo's amendment-kit-bench.md) flags every hunk and an empty commit range skips the item.
The `review_copy` write outside `audits/`, and the softened "never anywhere else" rule at :473 to 475, trace to no goal line.
Every agent that adds an own section needs a hand edit to synthesis's list; a CONTRACTS.md section 3 rule would scale with agent count.
The hand-mutant grep lives in four places with four patterns and scopes (review.md:212, gate-auditor.md:185, proof-runner.md:138, the known-bugs entry).
A config-free project no longer reviews as it did in 2.2.0 (untracked fence, four content triggers), and no file says so.
Every executing command comes from `.djinn/config.yaml`, which a reviewed branch can change.
The six new agents each copy the same five boilerplate blocks; a CONTRACTS.md "every review agent" section would cut about 250 lines.
add a CONTRACTS.md section on round n ownership: who writes status, who reports domain RESOLVED rules, which paths each agent gets.
a scripted dry run of review then dispatch round 2 on a fixture repo, asserting every prompt carries each key its Inputs section names.
a proof-runner fixture repo (Buffer growth past heap_mb, a hang past timeout_s, an ignored-file write, a node spawn with an empty env, a name with a space), each ending in its named verdict.
a preflight fixture repo (an unignored .env, 5,000 untracked files, a 200 MB untracked JSON, a file named with a space), asserting the patch holds no .env content and the run stops at step 3.
in CONTRACTS.md section 9, allow following a link from a fetched page only to a host the agent could have queried directly.
a relay security test, a tracked file named with a command substitution and an untracked one with a quote, run through a quick review, passing when no marker file exists afterward.
put the verdict word first in the gate table (gate-auditor.md:304) and the proof table (proof-runner.md:247).

give "Before the first live run" a leading readiness word and write an absent safety control as MISSING (live-system-reviewer.md:373), and add a held or BROKEN column to data-contract-reviewer's Stated invariants.
one comment line each in templates/config.yaml for cost.load bytes, gates guards, the heap_mb ceiling and the empty list to delete when uncommenting; make cost.limits entries objects.
move README.md:139's proof-runner paragraph under "Fix something it found" and show the direct and index routes with their report paths.
point both refusals (review.md:157, :440) at the commented template block and say each system needs name and code.
shorten relay.md:143's full row and README's four agent lines over 80 columns.
label project-specific examples as "example project", drop the work repo sentence (data-contract-reviewer.md:206), and refer to AUTOMATION.md generically.
CONTRACTS.md:295 gives the review_copy name as the system name only; review.md:417 adds live when there are several.
